updates.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5 — Near-Fable Performance at Half the Price
updates.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5 on July 24, 2026, positioning it as the new everyday workhorse for coding, agentic tasks, and scientific research. The model matches near-Fable 5 intelligence at half the cost ($5/$25 per million input/output tokens, unchanged from Opus 4.8), features a 1M-token context window, 128K max output tokens, and ships with thinking enabled by default plus a new effort-level toggle (low/medium/high/xhigh) so users can balance speed versus capability. Benchmarks show Opus 5 more than doubles Opus 4.8 on Frontier-Bench v0.1, comes within 0.5% of Fable 5 on CursorBench 3.2 at half the cost, scores 3× the next-best model on ARC-AGI 3, and tops Zapier's AutomationBench without consuming more tokens than prior Claude models. It is available immediately on the Claude API (claude-opus-5), Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry, claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork, and is the new default on Claude Max and the strongest model on Claude Pro.
updates.accuracy_notes: Confirmed by Anthropic's official announcement page, system card (www-cdn.anthropic.com), and independent coverage from Bloomberg, Axios, TechCrunch, Fortune, VentureBeat, SiliconANGLE, and 9to5Mac all dated July 24, 2026. Benchmark claims come from Anthropic and have not yet been independently replicated — note that early reviewers appear split on whether real-world performance matches the benchmarks. Pricing and availability details cross-verified across multiple sources.

updates.title: API: Opus 4.7 Fast Mode Removed; Mid-Conversation Tool Changes Beta Now Live
updates.summary: Two developer-facing API changes shipped alongside the Opus 5 launch on July 24, 2026. First, fast mode for Claude Opus 4.7 was permanently removed (it had been deprecated June 25): requests to claude-opus-4-7 with speed: 'fast' now return an error instead of silently falling back to standard speed — developers must migrate to Claude Opus 5 or Opus 4.8 to keep fast mode. Second, mid-conversation tool changes entered beta: on Fable 5, Mythos 5, Opus 4.8, and Opus 5, developers can now add or remove tools between conversation turns while preserving the prompt cache, enabling more dynamic agent architectures without re-establishing context. Additionally, the effort parameter on Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 defaults to high on both the Claude API and Claude Code.
updates.accuracy_notes: Opus 4.7 fast mode removal confirmed by multiple sources including byteiota.com, clskillshub.com, and releasebot.io all citing the same July 24, 2026 effective date. Mid-conversation tool changes and effort parameter details cross-verified via releasebot.io and developer coverage. All claims are consistent across sources and align with the official docs.anthropic.com API release notes page.

updates.title: I replaced Claude Code with a team of tiny specialists, and the boring setup worked better
updates.summary: An XDA Developers feature published July 24, 2026 details a developer's hands-on experiment replacing Claude Code with a multi-agent setup of smaller, specialized models for distinct sub-tasks (code review, test writing, documentation, etc.). The author finds that despite the less glamorous architecture, the 'boring' ensemble of tiny specialists outperformed a single Claude Code session in their workflow — surfacing broader questions about whether Claude Code's all-in-one approach is right for every project. The piece arrives one day after Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 launch and contributes to an ongoing conversation about the real-world utility of Claude Code as Anthropic continues to adjust its pricing and access policies.
